title: Iowa Counties: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility, 5 Measured | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Iowa counties of 50,000+ stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 55% of 228 sampled PDFs untagged, 17% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Iowa: Title II PDF backlog in counties of 50,000+
body:
Iowa has 10 counties of 50,000 or more residents with an official website listed in Wikidata. Under the ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H), counties of 50,000 or more must make web content, PDFs included, conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA by April 26, 2027; smaller Iowa counties, cities and special districts have until April 26, 2028.

Does ADA Title II apply to Iowa?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers Iowa's state agencies, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these counties link from their public websites. This page summarizes Iowa as a whole. It does not name or rank individual counties. For cities, see the city Backlog Index.

Iowa at a glance

  • 5 of 10 counties measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs); together they are home to about 480,000 residents. Of the rest, 2 blocked our crawler and 3 could not be sampled: too few PDFs on the main site (some host documents on other systems) or a crawl that only partly finished. That is not a clean result.
  • 228 PDFs analyzed. 54.8% had no accessibility tags, higher than the national figure of 45.1%. 16.7% were scanned images with no usable text, 59.7% did not declare a document language, and 64% had no document title.
  • Spread: in 2 of the 5 measured counties more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; in none, fewer than 1 in 10 were. The most common main issue was missing accessibility tags (4 of 5 counties).
  • 0 of 15 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured county has roughly 735 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured counties that is on the order of 4,500 pages.
  • 55% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for a Iowa county

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section.

For agendas, minutes and notices, our accessible meeting templates for small public bodies ($24, Word + PDF/UA) export tagged PDFs from Word, so new documents start out accessible.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.
